headline: A quick rain band and gusty winds arrive overnight, followed by a cooler weekend with a possible first frost.
summary: Thursday ended warm and mostly sunny, with clouds thickening this evening. A cold front, the leading edge of cooler air, moves through overnight and brings a fast band of rain into Friday morning. Rain totals should be light, mostly under about a quarter to a half inch, and some south Sound spots may stay mostly dry. Showers linger in the mountains and in a convergence zone over the central Puget Sound (where winds meet and push air upward) for much of Friday. Wind is the bigger story Friday. It picks up early in the morning, blows from the southwest, shifts to the west after the front passes, peaks from late morning into early afternoon, and eases Friday evening and overnight. Most areas should see gusts of 20 to 30 mph. Forecasters give a 50 to 70% chance of gusts above 45 mph along the Strait of Juan de Fuca, around Whidbey Island and Port Townsend, and at Point Roberts, so strong gusts are likely there but not certain. Temperatures drop noticeably behind the front. A weak disturbance brings a few light showers Saturday, ending Saturday night. Sheltered spots are getting close to frost, and Cascade valleys could touch freezing Sunday morning. That would be the season's first frost or freeze concern, but the chance of reaching 32°F or lower there is only about 30% and depends on how much the sky clears and whether fog forms. Early next week is drier and cool, then another system is expected Tuesday into Wednesday with more rain and breezy winds, though forecasters gave no details. No watches, warnings, or advisories apply to land areas. A Gale Warning and Small Craft Advisories cover the Strait and coastal and inland waters Friday, with ocean seas building to about 12 to 14 feet.
changes: Overnight and morning discussions described a weak front with rain lasting into Saturday and a Gale Watch. By afternoon the front was a faster, mostly Friday event with a clear gust threat (50 to 70% for gusts above 45 mph in the Strait area), and the Gale Watch became a Gale Warning. Morning fog advisories expired, Saturday rain was reduced to light showers, and the next system was stretched to Tuesday into Wednesday.
